articles.title: The two Christian saints who are the Buddha
articles.summary: The two Christian saints who are secretly the Buddha are Barlaam and Josaphat of India, a king's son who becomes a holy man despite being isolated from the outside world. This parallel to the story of the Buddha is no coincidence, as the story of Barlaam and Josaphat first appears in the Christian tradition in the 10th century, in Georgia as the Balavariani. The name "Budhasaf" in turn comes from the Persian version "Bodisav", and thence from the Sanskrit "Bodhisattva". This story was later adopted by Christian churches, including the Roman Catholic Church, and has been retold and translated in various forms, including a 1591 Japanese translation.
